title: Tailor a resume to a job posting
description: Map user intent to fundamental needs, process, handoffs, deliverables, UX, and outcome.

nodes.title: Job seeker
nodes.body: Has an existing resume and a target job posting. Wants a stronger application without inventing experience.

nodes.title: Understand what the role actually needs
nodes.body: Translate a noisy posting into the outcomes, skills, constraints, seniority signals, and evidence that matter most.

nodes.title: Stay truthful and defensible
nodes.body: Every tailored claim must be grounded in real experience the user can defend in an interview.

nodes.title: Spend effort where it changes the outcome
nodes.body: Prioritize high-impact changes instead of asking the user to rewrite everything for every application.

nodes.title: 1. Parse the job posting
nodes.body: Extract responsibilities, required capabilities, preferences, repeated themes, seniority cues, and likely evaluation criteria.

nodes.title: 2. Inventory resume evidence
nodes.body: Break the current resume into roles, accomplishments, skills, scope, metrics, domains, and keywords.

nodes.title: 3. Map requirements to evidence
nodes.body: For each meaningful requirement: matched, weakly matched, unsupported, or irrelevant. Rank by application impact.

nodes.title: 4. Draft targeted changes
nodes.body: Reorder, tighten, and rewrite bullets to foreground relevant evidence. Add terminology only when substantively true.

nodes.title: Posting → requirements model
nodes.body: The raw posting becomes a structured, prioritized set of needs that later steps can cite.

nodes.title: Requirements brief
nodes.body: A compact model of what matters most: top outcomes, skills, constraints, keywords, and evidence expectations.

nodes.title: Resume → evidence model
nodes.body: Resume claims become structured evidence with provenance back to the user’s source content.

nodes.title: Match / gap matrix
nodes.body: Requirement-by-requirement mapping with evidence, confidence, gaps, and recommended treatment.

nodes.title: Draft → human approval
nodes.body: Suggested edits remain proposed changes until the user reviews unsupported assumptions and wording changes.

nodes.title: Tailored resume
nodes.body: A ready-to-export resume emphasizing the strongest true evidence for this specific role.

nodes.title: Side-by-side source context
nodes.body: Keep the posting and resume visible beside extracted requirements and evidence so the user can verify reasoning quickly.

nodes.title: Evidence chips + confidence
nodes.body: Every recommendation shows why it exists, what source supports it, and whether the match is strong or tentative.

nodes.title: Prioritized actions, not a wall of edits
nodes.body: Lead with the few changes most likely to improve relevance. Separate critical fixes from optional polish.

nodes.title: Diff + approval gate
nodes.body: Show before/after text, let the user accept per change, and flag statements that may overreach the source resume.

nodes.title: Submit a stronger, truthful application
nodes.body: The final resume is more relevant to the target role, easy to defend in an interview, and faster to produce.
